title: Almighty Father, Heav’n and Earth
description: Almighty Father, Heav’n and Earth in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Edward Arthur Dayman wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 360.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Al-might-y Fa-ther, heav’n and earth With lav-ish wealth be-fore Thee bow; Those trea-sures owe to Thee their birth, Cre-a-tor, Ru-ler, Giv-er, Thou.

lines: Almighty Father, heav’n and earth
With lavish wealth before Thee bow;
Those treasures owe to Thee their birth,
Creator, Ruler, Giver, Thou.
The wealth of earth, of sky, of sea,
The gold, the silver, sparkling gem,
The waving corn, the bending tree,
Are Thine; to us Thou lendest them.
To Thee, as early morning’s dew,
Our praises, alms, and prayer shall rise,
As rose, when joyous earth was new,
Faith’s patriarchal sacrifice.
We, Lord, would lay, at Thy behest,
The costliest offerings on Thy shrine;
But when we give, and give our best,
We only give Thee what is Thine.
O Father, whence all blessings come,
O Son, Dispenser of God’s store,
O Spirit, bear our offerings home;
Lord, make them Thine forevermore.

licence: Public domain: Edward Arthur Dayman died in 1890.
credits: Words by Edward Arthur Dayman (1807–1890), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
